adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia
adds.summary: National framework page (applies to West Kalimantan, which records no separate regulation; the national position is what a visitor stands under). Indonesian law does not explicitly protect transgender people from discrimination or harassment, and the Constitution does not address sexual orientation or gender identity. On 14 December 2017 the Constitutional Court rejected 5-4 a conservative petition seeking to criminalise homosexuality and extramarital sex, declining to add them to the Penal Code. Transgender Indonesians who do not hide their identity often struggle to keep legitimate employment and can be pushed into sex work; a global survey cited on the page reports discrimination and harassment are not uncommon though direct violence is rare. The West Kalimantan division page records no separate LGBTI legislation or enforcement, so the national framework governs.
